reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports all key premises: it reports Hf-rich phase precipitation at interfaces, hindrance of grain boundary sliding and dislocation movement, improved high-temperature strength and ductility, unchanged room-temperature performance, and the study uses the same alloy system with Hf additions up to 0.8 at%. The hypothesis accurately represents these findings, though the specific 60–70% yield strength increase is a slight overstatement of the reported data (from 474 MPa baseline, the increase is less than 60% for the 0.5 at% Hf alloy).
premises: Hf addition to dual-phase refractory HEA forms fine Hf-rich precipitates at phase interfaces
These precipitates hinder dislocation motion and grain boundary sliding at high temperature
High-temperature strength and ductility improve markedly (60–70% yield strength increase)
Room-temperature performance remains similar to Hf-free baseline
Alloy density stays nearly unchanged with minor Hf addition
